correctness.rationale: The candidate density and uniform marginal identities follow by an exact beta integral for \(p>1\). The logarithmic potential \(L\) of the \(p=3\) density obeys distributional \(\Delta L=2\pi f_3\); \(f_3\) has an explicitly positive four-corner rectangle difference because \(u\mapsto(1-u)^{-1/3}\) is strictly convex, so \(L\) is not additively separable. Consequently a compactly supported smooth zero-marginal bump \(g\) has \(\int Lg\ne0\). The \(f_p\) density is uniformly positive on its compact support for \(p\in[2,3]\). Weak continuity \(p\to3\) plus uniform logarithmic-integrability near its singular kernel gives the exact \(\beta\downarrow0\) first-variation limit. A fixed sufficiently small signed bump amplitude \(t\) makes the normalized energy change converge to \(2t\int Lg+t^2\iint\log\|z-w\|_2\,g(z)g(w)\,dz\,dw>0\), hence strict improvement for all sufficiently small beta. The standalone diagnostic script reproduces the rational bound on the local density difference. No numerical experiment establishes the infinite interval.

value.rationale: This is a genuinely motivated negative resolution of the universal claim in Conjecture 9 of the original source: not merely a sample copula or a finite-grid variation, but an entire open exponent interval with the same smooth margin-preserving perturbation. It explains structurally why the attractive \(\(p=3\)-\beta\) geometric ansatz breaks down: log-potential equilibrium would force an additive Laplacian density, contradicted by the actual \(p=3\) copula density. The \(\beta=1\) positive theorem survives. An explicit beta threshold or optimizing copula would be a separate open problem.
